column5: A failed catalog fetch is converted into an empty list so every product listing reports no results instead of an error
column6: The SWR fetcher inside useInfiniteData at src/hooks/useInfiniteData.ts:65-79 returns res.data only when res.success is true - otherwise it logs to the console at :77 and returns an empty array at :78. Returning a value rather than throwing means SWR records a SUCCESS so the error field the hook exposes at :166 is never populated. The effect layer at :86-99 then reads swrResponse?.data || [] and swrResponse?.total || 0 - and because the fallback value is a bare array those both resolve to empty and zero. Downstream the search page destructures the hook at :150-156 and does not take error at all so it has nothing to render even if the hook had set it. Every listing built on this hook therefore renders its empty state on a backend failure. CLAUDE.md section 6.3 requires a distinct error state and explicitly forbids rendering a failed request as an empty result.
column10: Any catalog endpoint returning success false or failing - a 500 from the panel or a market with no permission to the requested scope.
column11: 1. Force /products to fail or return success false. 2. Open the search results page or any listing built on useInfiniteData. 3. Read what the page shows.
column12: The listing shows the error state with a retry - distinct from a genuine no-results outcome.
column13: The listing shows the empty state so the customer is told their search matched nothing when the request actually failed.
column14: Customers are told a category or search has no products whenever the backend fails - which hides outages - suppresses retries and looks like missing inventory. Because the hook backs every catalog listing the behaviour is repo wide rather than one screen.
column15: Throw from the fetcher when res.success is false so SWR populates error - then surface that error through the hook and render ErrorState with refetch at each consumer. Keep the empty state strictly for a successful response with zero items.

column5: Catalog SWR cache keys do not include the active market so a cached list survives a market switch
column6: useInfiniteData builds its cache key at src/hooks/useInfiniteData.ts:53-55 from the dataKey and a JSON serialisation of extraParams only. The market is never part of it - it travels as the X-Market header applied by the interceptor - so two different markets produce the SAME key for the same listing and the second market reads the first market payload straight from cache. No SWR key anywhere in src includes a market value which was confirmed across all 29 files that call useSWR. The search page shows the pattern at :158 where dataKey is /productsSearch: plus the query - specific about the query and blind to the market. This is the mechanism underneath issue 1 but it is a DIFFERENT root cause and needs a different fix - issue 1 is that resolveMarketForCountry only revalidates the settings key while this is that the keys are not market scoped in the first place. Fixing either one alone leaves the other as a latent trap.
column10: Two markets with differing catalogue or pricing and a user who switches market after browsing.
column11: 1. Browse a category or run a search in market A. 2. Switch to market B. 3. Return to the same listing without a hard reload and read the cached results.
column12: The cache key carries the market so a switch produces a different key and the listing refetches under the new X-Market header.
column13: The key is identical across markets so the previous market cached payload is served.
column14: Wrong market inventory and pricing shown after a switch. Making the key market aware fixes the whole class at once rather than requiring every future switch site to remember to invalidate.
column15: Include the active market code in the SWR key for every market-scoped fetch - either by adding it to extraParams in useInfiniteData or by prefixing dataKey with the market. That way a switch changes the key and no explicit invalidation is needed.

column5: The documented per-volatility stale times are not implemented for any catalog fetch
column6: CLAUDE.md section 7.3 sets a stale time per data type - product lists about 2 minutes - product detail and reviews about 5 minutes - categories brands stores and settings about 30 minutes - and instructs that dedupingInterval and revalidateOnFocus must be set per volatility rather than accepting defaults. Across the 29 files that call useSWR only 3 set dedupingInterval and all three are account screens - src/pages/my-account/orders/index.tsx - wishlists/index.tsx and notifications/index.tsx. No catalog fetch sets it - useInfiniteData passes only revalidateOnFocus and revalidateOnMount at src/hooks/useInfiniteData.ts:80-83 - so every catalog list - product detail - category - brand and store request falls back to the SWR default deduping window of 2 seconds instead of the documented minutes. The focus half of the rule is largely done - 25 of the 29 files do set revalidateOnFocus - so this is specifically about the stale windows.

column11: 1. Open a listing and navigate away and back within a minute. 2. Watch the network panel. 3. Observe the catalog request is re-issued rather than served from cache for the documented window.
column12: Catalog requests are deduplicated for the window the documentation specifies per data type.
column13: Requests are deduplicated for only 2 seconds so browsing re-fetches near-static data such as categories and brands repeatedly.
column14: Avoidable request volume against the panel on the busiest screens and slower navigation for the customer - most wastefully on categories brands and stores which the documentation treats as changing about every 30 minutes.
column15: Set dedupingInterval per the section 7.3 table at each catalog call site or centrally in useInfiniteData with a per-data-type override - and keep the revalidateOnFocus values already in place.

column5: Debug logging scaffolding was left in the product page server render path
column6: The product detail getServerSideProps at src/pages/products/[slug]/index.tsx:288-345 contains five console.log calls added for debugging - a decorative banner reading ========== SSR PRODUCT PAGE ========== at :300 - the requested slug at :301 - a product existence flag at :309 - the product slug at :313 and a call labelled Fetched Product Full at :318 which passes JSON.stringify(data?.initialProduct?.slug - null - 2) so despite the label it prints only the slug and formats a plain string with indentation. This runs on every server render of the most requested page on the storefront. compiler.removeConsole in next.config.ts strips console.log from production builds so the runtime cost is limited to development and to any build where that option changes - but the block is debugging scaffolding rather than intended logging and the misleading label invites a future reader to trust it.
